method.model: ONE Analog Devices TMP36 temperature sensor, explicitly declared by the inventor, whose output voltage V_OUT (in mV, relative to the sensor's ground pin) is the inventor's own declared value. The NOMINAL output characteristic of the TMP36 relates that voltage to a temperature on the Celsius scale: 500 mV at 0 degrees Celsius and 10 mV per degree Celsius. The result is the nominal temperature of that relation only, not a measured, calibrated, accurate or guaranteed device temperature.
method.executed_form: t_celsius = (v_out - 500) / 10, with v_out in mV inside the nominal-model interval 100 to 1750 mV inclusive, decided from the exact decimal value before any binary rounding; evaluated as the exact rational value of the binary64 input rounded once to binary64 and accepted only when it is exactly 0.0 for exactly 500 mV, or finite, nonzero, of the exact result's sign, within a relative error of 2^-52 of it and inside -40 to 125; then shown only when it agrees with the exact decimal relation of the entered value within 2^-45 degrees Celsius, as that exact decimal value.
method.derivation: Analog Devices TMP35/TMP36/TMP37 data sheet, Rev. H: Table 4 (printed page 8) gives the TMP36 output characteristics as an offset voltage of 0.5 V, an output voltage scaling of 10 mV per degree Celsius and an output voltage of 750 mV at 25 degrees Celsius; Table 1 (printed page 3) gives the TMP36 scale factor of 10 mV per degree Celsius over -40 to +125 degrees Celsius and the typical TMP36 output voltage of 750 mV at 25 degrees Celsius; page 1 states the TMP36 is specified from -40 to +125 degrees Celsius (ADI-S1). From these InventorAI writes V_OUT = 500 mV + (10 mV per degree Celsius) x T and solves it for T; the data sheet is not claimed to print this solved form. Applying the relation to -40 and +125 degrees Celsius gives the nominal-model interval 100 mV to 1750 mV. The relation is restated independently; no data-sheet text, table, figure, model or code is copied, and the nominal relation is not shown to describe the inventor's device.

roles.meaning: the TMP36 output voltage relative to its ground pin, as declared by the inventor; not sampled, measured or checked by InventorAI (the role written V_OUT)

the NOMINAL temperature on the Celsius scale given by the nominal TMP36 relation for the declared voltage; signed, exactly zero at 500 mV; never a measured, calibrated, accurate or guaranteed device temperature, rating or limit (the role written T)

rules: Grammar: strict unsigned ASCII decimal digits with an optional single fractional part of one to three digits; no sign, plus sign, exponent, separator, Unicode digit, unit suffix, inf, nan or normalization. An omitted, malformed or over-length value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called.

Nominal-model interval: the exact decimal value of v_out must lie between 100 mV and 1750 mV inclusive, decided before any binary rounding; outside it the outcome is OUTSIDE_NOMINAL_MODEL_RANGE with no number. The interval is the nominal relation applied to the stated TMP36 specified temperature range of -40 to +125 degrees Celsius. It is NOT the data sheet's electrical output-voltage range specification and NOT a claim of guaranteed device accuracy.

Owner applicability: the shared owner declines a v_out that is not greater than zero as UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE / INPUT_OUTSIDE_ADMITTED_RANGE, shown as the neutral UNMAPPED_OWNER_OUTCOME (unreachable from the page); a value outside the nominal-model interval that reaches the method adapter is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

Binary bridge: the admitted decimal is converted once to the correctly rounded binary64 value; the interval ends 100 and 1750 are exact in binary64 and rounding is monotonic, so an admitted value stays inside the interval and exactly 500 mV stays exactly 500.

Numerical acceptance in the adapter: the exact rational value (v_out - 500) / 10 of the binary input is rounded once to binary64. Exactly 500 mV gives exactly 0.0. A nonzero exact result is accepted only when the rounded value is finite, nonzero, of the same sign, within a relative error of 2^-52 of it and inside -40 to 125; otherwise FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload, never rewritten as a refusal.

Decimal-reference acceptance in the consumer: a successful owner result is shown only when it is exactly zero for exactly 500 mV, and otherwise has the sign of, and lies within 2^-45 degrees Celsius of, the exact decimal value (V_OUT - 500) / 10 of the entered decimal; otherwise the outcome is KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE with no number. The proven worst case for every admitted input is 1.3 x 2^-46 degrees Celsius.

Display: the accepted result is shown as the exact decimal value of the nominal relation for the entered decimal, with at least one and at most four digits after the decimal point; no rounding is needed or applied. The number of digits shown implies no measurement resolution, precision or accuracy.
The 64-character field cap is for abuse and resource protection only; it is NON-PHYSICAL and is not the admitted engineering domain.

disclosure: This is the nominal temperature that the TMP36 relation gives for the output voltage V_OUT you entered: T = (V_OUT − 500 mV) / (10 mV/°C).
The voltage is your own declared value. InventorAI did not read, sample or measure your sensor and does not check the value or that the sensor is a TMP36.

It is the nominal relation only. A real TMP36 can differ from it by several degrees, as its data sheet specifies, and no accuracy, linearity, self-heating, calibration, instrument or ADC error is included.

The accepted voltage interval, 100 mV to 1750 mV, is the nominal relation applied to the sensor's specified range of −40 °C to +125 °C. It is not the data sheet's output-voltage specification and does not mean the device is accurate inside it.
The number of digits shown follows from your entry; it is not the precision of the sensor or of any measurement.
It is preliminary, advisory, UNVALIDATED and not evidence, and it must be confirmed by measurement before any reliance; it says nothing about sensor choice, suitability or safety.

sources.inspected_content: Supports only, for the TMP36: Table 4, TMP35/TMP36/TMP37 Output Characteristics (Theory of Operation, printed page 8 of 19): offset voltage 0.5 V, output voltage scaling 10 mV per degree Celsius, output voltage at 25 degrees Celsius 750 mV - the nominal output characteristic; Table 1, Specifications (printed page 3 of 19, conditions VS = 2.7 V to 5.5 V and -40 to +125 degrees Celsius unless noted): Scale Factor, TMP36, 10 mV per degree Celsius (typical) over -40 to +125 degrees Celsius, and TMP36 Output Voltage 750 mV (typical) at 25 degrees Celsius; page 1 (Features and General Description): the TMP36 is specified from -40 to +125 degrees Celsius. Recorded as limits of the nominal model, NOT applied: Table 1 also gives accuracy specifications of +/-1 to +/-4 degrees Celsius (typical and maximum, by grade and temperature), typical linearity of 0.5 degrees Celsius, a supply range of 2.7 to 5.5 V and a separate Output Voltage Range specification of 100 to 2000 mV; Table 1 note 1 states that the specifications do not consider errors caused by self-heating. The nominal-model interval of this method is derived from the nominal relation at -40 and +125 degrees Celsius and is distinct from that Output Voltage Range specification.
